title: Config-driven embedding + reranker quality gates and drift detection playbook
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Problem: We frequently ship model/config changes (quantization profile, batch limits, reranker weights, embedding model variants). There is no single, automated gate that ties those changes to the embedding+rerank offline quality checks and drift detectors. Result: occasional regressions in recall/precision surfaced by customers or found in postmortems.

Goal: Build a config-driven evaluation and gating pipeline that runs for every model/config change PR and produces a human- and machine-readable verdict. The pipeline must: 1) run fast sanity checks, 2) run a wider offline regression suite (recall@k, precision@k, NDCG) against canonical test sets, 3) compute drift statistics on embedding distributions and reranker score distributions, 4) produce alerts and block merges for severe regressions, 5) provide canary rollout guidance and automatic rollback metadata for Console.

Scope: The first iteration focuses on embeddings + rerankers used by Search and Recommendations workloads: embedding model variants, embedding dimension/quantization configs, and reranker checkpoint swaps or hyperparameter changes.

Success metrics:
- False negative rate for blocking regressions <= 5% on historical regression set.
- CI runtime for the fast gate <= 12 minutes on our dedicated CI pool.
- Drift alert precision > 90% (measured on labeled drift incidents).

Proposed approach: 
1) Define three-tier gates: 
   - Fast sanity gate (CI): token-limited recall@10 / precision@10 on 200 representative queries + embedding norm checks and embedding centroid cosine similarity vs baseline. Runs on PRs.
   - Offline regression suite (scheduled or triggered on richer changes): full holdout datasets (10k queries) measuring recall@k, NDCG@10, reranker AUC, and ranking correlation (Kendall tau) vs baseline. Produces a detailed report with effect sizes and per-segment breakdowns.
   - Drift detector (monitoring): continuous windowed checks on production traffic —distributional divergence (Wasserstein on pairwise distances), embedding centroid cosine, embedding norm histogram KL divergence, and reranker score shift. Generates alerts when thresholds crossed or statistically significant p-values reported.

2) Thresholds and alert policy: start with conservative thresholds derived from historical deltas: recall@10 drop of >2.5% absolute OR NDCG@10 drop >1.5% triggers offline regression; >5% absolute recall drop or reranker AUC drop >3% => block and require escalation. Drift detector uses dynamic baselines with weekly retrain windows and triggers warning/critical levels.

3) Automation & CI integration: a CI job that runs the fast gate on every model/config PR; results posted back to GitHub PR with a standardized verdict (PASS/WARN/FAIL) and an artifact link to the offline report. A merge is blocked on FAIL. Offline suite runs as a required job for changes touching embedding/reranker config files (paths: /models/embeddings/*, /models/rerank/*) or changes to runtime-1.25 quantization knobs.

4) Reporting artifacts & dashboards: store reports as JSONL in bucket gs://redwood-evals/<model>/<date>/report.jsonl and index in the Console quality dashboard. Provide a short explainer text and top 10 failing queries. Link to reproducible evaluation code in GitHub.

5) Fallbacks & runbook: if CI shows FAIL, default to blocking. For deploy-time regressions detected by monitoring, the Console should support an automatic rollback to the most recent passing pinned model with an incident ticket template prefilled.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Fast gate implemented as a CI job that runs within 12m for representative PRs and posts verdicts to PRs.
- Offline suite produces JSON reports with standardized keys (metrics, deltas, artifacts) and a human-readable summary page.
- Monitoring drift detectors are implemented and wired to the Console alerting with warning/critical thresholds.
- Playbook documented (Confluence) with runbook for on-call and a postmortem checklist.

- Draft playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Reranker+Quality+Playbook

comments: 2026-03-01 — Marco Ruiz: Spiked a fast CI job using 200-sample set. Median runtime 9m on c5-dedicated CI runners. Uploaded initial prototype at PR #519.
2026-03-03 — Dana Lee (Data Science): Reviewed fast gate metrics. Suggested replace average similarity with trimmed-mean to reduce sensitivity to long-tail queries.
2026-03-05 — Aisha Patel: Implemented trimmed-mean change and updated thresholds. Re-ran prototype; false positives dropped from 8% to 3% on historical regressions set.
2026-03-07 — QA: Added reproducibility checklist to offline suite. Need to validate storage retention policy for reports (30d vs 90d).
2026-03-09 — Marco Ruiz: Wired WARN to Console dashboard and created alert playbook stub. Next: complete automated rollback integration with Console release manager.
notes: Trade-offs considered: stricter thresholds reduce customer impact but increase CI churn. We opt for conservative fast gate to catch large regressions and leave nuanced regressions to offline suite.
Open questions: whether to include embedding quantization artifact digest in the report to ensure exact reproducibility, and which jobs are allowed to override block (SRE emergency process).
Implementation owners: Embeddings infra (Aisha) for CI and monitoring hooks; Evals infra (Marco) for offline suite and report schema; Console (Jin Park) for alerting and rollback UI.
Estimated infra cost: incremental storage ~7GB/month, CI minutes ~1500 minutes/month for active teams; billing ticket to be created if we scale beyond prototype.
